info.title: Bibleit REST API
info.description: Versioned REST surface with distinct organization service-token and personal bearer authentication. Organization routes require Authorization: Bearer svc_<secret>. Personal routes require existing finite bt_ API/CLI tokens; browser sessions are not accepted. Organization ownership, current status, scopes, processing rules and quotas apply. JSON bodies are bounded to 16 KiB except full presentation PUT, whose transport limit is 2,016,384 bytes and whose document limit is 2,000,000 encoded JSON bytes. Unknown body fields and unknown query fields are rejected. All responses are no-store. Rate limiting is node-local (120 requests/minute per authenticated principal plus existing peer/global admission). Duplicate-sensitive creation POSTs support optional Idempotency-Key with a 24-hour atomic replay contract. Unsupported REST operations reject the header with 422. Credential issuance/rotation and one-use downloads never replay secrets or streams. Service-token PATCH and rotation require strong configuration validators. Catalogue discovery is distinct from enabled libraries. Library PUT accepts an empty JSON object and never downloads content. Organization identity and active memberships require explicit organization.get and membership scopes. Live metadata PATCH edits the name. Live workspace PUT requires a source live.move token and a destination live.create token in X-Destination-Service-Token. Both mutations require the latest Live If-Match validator. Live scripture queue items have stable persisted IDs and zero-based positions. Queue writes use the shared Live If-Match validator. Ordered pagination rejects cursor use after a sequence change. Organization Live Studio GET/PUT use explicit live_studio.get/update scopes and strong settings ETags. PUT preserves the existing complete-settings validation and revision increments; saves notify Lives after commit. Organization presentations support paginated CRUD with strong document ETags. Presentation display PUT requires presentation.present, an explicit current saved revision and the Live If-Match validator; draft saves never publish. Raw binary asset uploads and portable ZIP imports are exceptions to JSON transport limits; require Content-Length, identity encoding and scoped authorization. Assets remain bearer-protected and support single byte ranges. Imports create a new unpublished presentation atomically. Presentation exports are asynchronous requester-private saved-revision jobs. POST their downloads collection with an empty JSON object to consume and stream a completed file once; GET never consumes exports. No ranges or automatic retries for export downloads. Personal /me and /accounts expose only the caller’s personal identity/account. Personal library, scripture and Live routes bind that account explicitly. Personal tokens cannot authenticate organization management, presentations, Studio or workspace moves. Shared Live/control routes select credential type and enforce account ownership. Personal Live DELETE requires If-Match. Tokens are checked freshly after queue/lock waits and at final commits; existing personal scope inheritance and fifteen-minute rotation overlap remain unchanged. No delegated OAuth is implied. Registered public clients can now use Authorization Code with S256 PKCE and explicit browser consent for personal access. Metadata is /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; OAuth protocol routes stay on https://bibleit.app/oauth, outside the API origin. Opaque oa_ access tokens last at most 15 minutes; optional offline_access enables single-use rotating refresh tokens within a fixed 30-day grant. Code or refresh replay revokes the grant. Existing bt_ and svc_ rules are unchanged. Versioned operator realtime delivery is GET /lives/{live_id}/events with optional opaque after cursor and wait=0..25 seconds. It returns current snapshots or a heartbeat, never a durable event log. Current bearer secret identity, scopes, account ownership and processing policy are checked before delayed delivery. Operator watches do not consume audience seats. The Fern reference is configured for the bibleit organization. SDK generation is maintained separately in bibleit-go. Browser API Explorer execution is disabled: the current API has no cross-origin browser contract or documentation credential proxy. Copy the HTTP examples into a backend or CLI client. The API origin serves the latest major version without a prefix (currently v1), while /v1 stays pinned. Production integrations should use the explicit major version. The existing https://bibleit.app/api/v1 URL remains supported. API-host resource links pin /v1, including links returned through the latest alias. Documentation is hosted at https://docs.bibleit.dev; https://api.bibleit.app/docs redirects there.

delete.description:
Delete all Lives in the service token's organization in one account-locked transaction. Current authority is rechecked after lock acquisition; foreign organizations return 404. Returns 200 with the actual `deleted` count, including zero. No per-Live `If-Match` is used. Concurrent creation serializes on the account lock; session shutdown follows committed deletion. `Idempotency-Key` is unsupported. put.description:
**Required scopes:** `live.update`.

Service ownership, current explicit scopes and processing policy are checked inside the serialized Live actor. Requires live.update plus translation.read for scripture or presentation.present for saved-deck publication. Updates persist before broadcasting. Shared Live sequence validators protect display/playback/metadata/queue changes; viewer counts do not. Presentation publication requires presentation_id and explicit current saved revision. Foreign decks return 404, changed/missing requested revision returns 409 presentation_revision_conflict (no historical revision archive), empty decks/stopped Lives return 409. A fresh immutable snapshot is captured, and the deck revision is rechecked under the same workspace lock as final Live save/media pins, so a concurrent deck change cannot silently publish newer content. Optional slide_id selects a stable slide. When updating the same deck already in Presentation mode, omitted slide_id preserves the selected stable ID when present (otherwise clamps the prior index), and blank/paused state are retained. A new presentation starts at slide zero unless selected explicitly. Saving drafts never publishes; source deletion leaves existing snapshots intact. Empty display clears scripture and switches to Reader without deleting a retained presentation snapshot. Also accepts finite personal bearer tokens for resources owned by the caller’s personal account. Personal tokens cannot operate organization Lives, use collaborators’/children’s authority, or publish presentations. Current personal token scopes and user permissions are rechecked after waits. put.description:
**Required scopes:** `live.move`.

Requires the source Authorization bearer with live.move and a destination X-Destination-Service-Token with live.create. Both credentials are revalidated after acquiring sorted workspace locks. Destination mismatch, expiry/revocation or missing destination credential returns 403. Destination total Live quota applies; exhausted capacity or same-workspace requests return 409. Missing/foreign source Lives return 404. Only organization-to-organization moves are supported. Ownership and cleared payloads commit in one transaction before disconnecting viewers and management watchers. Clears scripture payload/reference and presentation snapshots/media pins, resets to hidden Reader mode with pause off, removes collaborators and revokes pending Live invitations. Replaces translation selections and viewer limit with destination library/quota. Existing audience secrets are invalidated while preserving protection. Name, lifecycle status, runtime and viewer styling remain. Returns destination-owned Live and new ETag; source-only credentials lose access. On an ambiguous timeout, inspect through the destination token before retrying. A retry using the old source organization returns 404 once moved.

LiveEvent.description: Event schema major version 1. Snapshot on connection/reconnection; changed snapshot when comparison differs; null-data heartbeat at wait expiry. Notifications may coalesce, repeat or be missed. Not exactly-once and no historical replay.

next_cursor.description: Required opaque continuation cursor. Null only on the last page; otherwise pass unchanged as after. Carries no authority.

ScriptureBookRead.description: One bounded book page, always paginated: default 50, maximum 500 verses, and at most 3MiB serialized JSON including metadata. The byte budget can return fewer verses with nonnull next_cursor. Stable chapter/verse order; no totals or unbounded mode.

Problem.description: Error response. 400 malformed JSON; 401 invalid/expired/revoked token; 403 denied scope or domain policy; 404 unknown/foreign resource; 405 unsupported method; 409 quota/conflict or stopped Live; 412 stale state validator; 428 missing If-Match; 413 body too large; 415 unsupported media type; 422 invalid fields; 429 admission budget exhausted; 503 unavailable dependency.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional case-sensitive retry key, retained 24 hours from successful commit. Scoped to credential principal (stable service-token ID; personal bt_ credential; delegated OAuth grant), account and concrete method/path. Payload, If-Match, query string and Content-Type must match. JSON object key order is ignored; queue reference casing/defaults are normalized; raw upload/import bytes are hashed. Replays retain original success body, Location and ETag with a fresh X-Request-Id, after current authority/ownership/processing/library checks. Same scope/key with changed input:409 idempotency_conflict. Concurrent requests serialize; a contended retry lock can return 409 idempotency_in_progress; bounded database waits can return 503. Errors are not recorded. After expiry, a key is treated as new; original resource/job lifetime is unchanged. No key means no retry guarantee.
